item.title: Big Changes Coming to Shared Mobility
item.description:
Big changes are coming to shared mobility in Columbus! As our city continues to grow, we’re committed to making it easier, safer, and more convenient for you to get where you need to go.

We’re thrilled to announce upcoming enhancements to our shared mobility options, giving you more flexibility and access than ever before. Whether you bike, scoot, or rely on other forms of shared transportation, these updates are designed with you in mind.

Special Offer for Former CoGo Members!

As part of this transition, Veo is offering 6-month memberships to VeoPlus for all qualifying former CoGo members—a $48 value! This means more access, more convenience, and more ways to ride.

Riders can learn more and sign up here

Stay connected for updates, and get ready to experience a better way to move through Columbus!

item.title: Bike Plus Plan Adopted! More Exciting Things Coming in 2025
item.description:
City Council officially adopted the Bike Plus Plan in December! Thank you to everyone who was involved in shaping the Bike Plus Plan by sharing your lived experience, feedback and support. The final plan and bikeways Vision Network maps are available for viewing here.

Implementing the Bike Plus Plan will be a phased, multi-year process that hinges on funding, collaboration, feasibility and ongoing performance metrics. Several strategies are already underway to support biking, scooting and rolling, including:

  • Formalizing a Complete Streets Policy
  • Creating a Bikeways and Operations Maintenance Policy
  • Updating the Regional Bikeways Map both in print and online

Have you seen the safety improvements on East Broad Street?

The City received a federal Safe Streets for All grant to make safety improvements along East Broad Street, including a demonstration project to add protected bike lanes from Parsons Avenue to Nelson Road. We are testing three types of barrier materials that separate the bike lanes from vehicle lanes, along with two bus pads at high-frequency transit stops. If you ride on East Broad, please share your feedback via our survey! To take the survey, scan the QR code on the signs located near bus stops along the corridor.

Look for our newsletter next month to learn more about our shared mobility improvements coming this spring!

Questions or comments?

Contact the City of Columbus Mobility Team at bikeways@columbus.gov.

item.title: View the Bike Plus draft plan and attend the City Council hearing Dec. 3
item.description:
Thanks to your passion and participation, we are excited to have a draft Bike Plus Plan! The draft plan and bikeways vision network maps are available for viewing here. We have been working hard over the past 18 months to develop goals and strategies incorporating thousands of your comments and technical expertise. You can add comments on the project website or by emailing bikeways@columbus.gov.

City Council will hold a public hearing on the draft Bike Plus Plan on Tuesday, Dec. 3, at 5 p.m. in Council Chambers. The Bike Plus team will present the draft plan, share what we heard from the community and discuss strategies. All written testimonies must be submitted by noon the day of the hearing to ASLemus@columbus.gov.

We look forward to hearing from you and to implementing the Bike Plus Plan!

item.title: What do you think? Share feedback on the Bike Plus Draft Vision Network!
item.description:
Thank you so much for sharing your thoughts throughout this process, whether that was through surveys, in-person engagement events or during Community Conversations. Based on feedback from the community, we have developed a draft vision network of bikeways including proposed locations and types of bikeways. 

Give input on the draft vision network

Please help spread the word about the Bike Plus Draft Vision Network to your friends, family, and neighbors. The draft vision network will be available for comment through the month of June. The feedback we receive will help the City develop a plan that reflects your needs and experiences.

In the spring we held Open Houses and numerous Community Conversations. Key feedback gained included:

  • More separation between different types of modes (bikes, scooters, pedestrians and vehicles)
  • Open to parking removal if bikeways were implemented in return
  • Increase maintenance for sidewalks, bike lanes, snow removal and road resurfacing
  • Interest in bike parking for all types of bikes and scooters
  • Desire for more policies and programs promoting biking.

Want to get more involved? The Bike Plus project team will be holding pop-up events throughout the city this summer. At these events, residents will have the opportunity to provide feedback on the draft vision network, learn more about the project, ask questions and continue to share their ideas for making biking, scooting, skating and rolling safer in Columbus.

Can’t make the summer engagement events? Visit our website for project updates. We appreciate your input and help spreading the word about Bike Plus!

item.title: City of Columbus Bikeways Draft Vision Network Ready for Public Comment
item.description:
For Immediate Release

June 3, 2024

Contact: Debbie Briner

614-645-6467

dsbriner@columbus.gov

 

Web – Facebook – Twitter

City of Columbus Bike Plus Draft Vision Network Ready for Public Feedback

Residents have an opportunity through June to share their comments on an interactive map of the draft vision network developed by the City of Columbus Bike Plus planning initiative. The Bike Plus Plan, led by the Department of Public Service, will improve and expand connections that support safe and comfortable travel in the city by biking, scooting and rolling.

The draft vision network outlines proposed route improvements for safe and equitable city bikeway infrastructure that includes separated bikeways such as shared-use paths and protected on-street lanes, bike lanes or buffered lanes, bike boulevards and trails. A glossary that defines these types of bikeway infrastructure is available on the Bike Plus website here.

“We are eager to hear from the public on the Bike Plus draft vision network—shaped largely by earlier community engagement—to help the city advance a bikeways plan that connects neighborhoods and increases safe access to work, school, entertainment and other amenities and services,” said Public Service Director Kelly Scocco. “Bike Plus will make it more convenient and comfortable to get around Columbus without a car, for equitable and sustainable transportation.”

The Bike Plus planning process launched in 2023. An initial interactive map sought residents’ input to help identify locations where they face challenges and barriers to biking, scooting and rolling, such as safety concerns due to fast-moving vehicle traffic and missing bikeway or trail and path connections.

In addition, the Bike Plus planning team gathered community input through an online survey, pop-up events, a workshop with stakeholders, a series of public office hours, and four open houses this spring where residents could mark up maps to help develop the draft vision network with potential priority projects and policy recommendations.

All of this community engagement helped to shape the draft vision network. Now, residents can provide feedback again on the proposed bikeway projects shown on the draft network’s interactive map.

The final Bike Plus Plan will consider this public feedback and the city’s technical review and feasibility analysis that is currently in progress. Bikeway infrastructure projects will be identified where they are most needed for completion in the short term, and other connections will be completed as the full network is built out over the coming years.

The draft vision network focuses on City of Columbus bikeways infrastructure. Connections with neighboring communities will be coordinated with those jurisdictions.

A finalized Bike Plus Plan will be presented to City Council later this year for proposed adoption.

item.title: Please help us shape our emerging plan recommendations!
item.description:
Share your input by attending a Bike Plus Open House!

During these meetings, you can expect to establish a vision network, discuss prioritization and advise on policy recommendations. Everything will be in draft form, but we are excited to be working collaboratively with our partners and the public in creating Bike Plus.  

Since summer 2023 the Bike Plus team has had over 6,800 engagement touchpoints through 88 outreach activities. During engagement, we heard about the top barriers to biking and rolling including fast-moving vehicle traffic, missing bikeways or trail/paths and concerns about personal safety.  

When asked to identify specific areas in Columbus, streets that received the most comments regarding barriers included High Street, Indianola Avenue and Cleveland Avenue. The map below highlights areas where the most comments were received. The darker and thicker the line, the more comments the street received.

item.title: We appreciate your input, here’s what we’ve heard!
item.description:
Thank you so much for sharing your thoughts this fall via the Bike Plus survey, Interactive Map, and pop-up events at various community hubs. Through these activities we’ve received over 6,000 comments from people across the city about challenges involved in biking, scootering, and skating, and what they want to see changed. Top concerns expressed in the survey include not feeling safe near fast moving cars (84%), not enough connections to trails, bikeways, and sidewalks (75%) and not enough trails, bikeways, or sidewalks in my neighborhood (50%). 

We also asked people “What excites you most about this plan?” and respondents mentioned: 

  • Safer bicycle facilities 
  • A more connected network with  separated bicycle lanes 
  • An integrated transit system 
  • A decrease in car dependency 

We have begun developing draft recommendations, based on a combination of community input and the technical analysis conducted thus far. There will be additional engagement opportunities in spring 2024, which we will share in the next newsletter. We look forward to continuing the conversation! 

Visit our website for project updates. We appreciate your input and help spreading the word about Bike Plus! 

It's that time of year to bundle up! You don’t have to stop bicycling just because it’s winter! Central Ohio Greenways has many tips on how to stay safe and warm this winter.

item.title: Where should we build future bikeways?
item.description:
Thank you so much for sharing your thoughts via the Bike Plus survey. We heard from over 3,100 people across the City! 89% of people said they want to bike more and 74% want to walk more. However, 68% said it is currently difficult to get around Columbus on a bike, scooter or other small-wheeled device. Respondents let us know they want better infrastructure, increased connections between trails, bikeways and sidewalks, and increased safety near fast-moving traffic.

We will be using this information to help develop a vision statement and a set of draft goals. This qualitative input will also be used in combination with the technical analysis currently underway, to begin developing Bike Plus draft recommendations. There will be additional engagement opportunities throughout the Bike Plus process (see below) and we look forward to continuing the conversation!

We are announcing the Bike Plus Interactive Map, where you can give input on specific locations where improvements could make it more comfortable to bike, scoot, skate and roll: https://tooledesign.github.io/Columbus_BMP/

Please help spread the word about the Interactive Map to your friends, family and neighbors. The feedback we receive will help the City develop a plan that reflects your needs and experiences.

Want to get more involved? The Bike Plus project team will be setting up booths at locations across the city throughout November and December. At these events, residents will have the opportunity to learn more about the project, ask questions and share their ideas for making biking, scootering and skating safer in Columbus.

Visit our website to see a list of event locations and for other project updates. We appreciate your input and help spreading the word about Bike Plus!

item.title: We need you to be involved in Bike Plus!
item.description:
The City of Columbus has started the planning process to improve how we bike, scooter and skate – however you choose to roll – in Columbus. We’re calling the plan “Bike Plus” – and we need your help!

What is the Bike Plus Plan?

Bike Plus is a plan by the City of Columbus to create a safe, connected, and comfortable network for people to bike, scooter, skate and roll in the city. Through transportation improvements like protected bike lanes, trail connections, and crosswalks, we can make it more convenient, safe and enjoyable to get around Columbus without a car. This plan will identify where these improvements are most needed to connect community members to the places they need and want to go.

Why does this plan matter?

The goal of Bike Plus is to make travel safer in all neighborhoods, but particularly in the Vision Zero High Injury Network and in Communities of Interest. Compared to other neighborhoods, people living in Communities of Interest may have fewer choices about how, when and where they travel, putting them at higher risk as they move around.

We know we need to provide more safe and viable options. This planning process will prioritize community voices to inform how we can reduce barriers to these options and make a direct impact on how we travel and connect with each other across Columbus.

How Can I Help?

 

Take our survey to help us better understand your experiences and goals to bike, scooter, skate and roll in Columbus.

 

Share our survey with your friends, family, and colleagues – we need to hear from as many people as possible to create an effective, impactful plan. Our survey is also available in Somali and Spanish!

 

Visit our website for project information, updates and events. We will need feedback at multiple points during this 18-month planning process – so let’s keep the conversation going!
